title: PowerShell spawns nested PowerShell that Start-Process-es a .bat from ExternalPayloads
source: ML-style review of Wazuh archives.json (events with no corresponding alerts.json entry)
description: powershell.exe (user HVAN\Administrator, integrity High) launched a child powershell.exe with command line `powershell.exe & {Start-Process "C:\AtomicRedTeam\atomics\..\ExternalPayloads\T1059.003_script.bat"}` (path traversal '..' in the path, payload folder 'ExternalPayloads'). In both runs the .bat did not exist (console: 'The system cannot find the file specified'), so no cmd.exe batch child was created, but the execution attempt itself is the malicious behaviour. The only alert Wazuh raised in that second was 92213 on the __PSScriptPolicyTest .ps1 temp file (context event) – not the process creation.
why_wazuh_missed: Wazuh's Sysmon rules (92xxx) cover cmd.exe / net.exe / discovery children but there is no rule for PowerShell → PowerShell Start-Process of a script file.
detection_hints_for_rule: Sysmon EID 1: parentImage ends with \powershell.exe AND image ends with \powershell.exe AND commandLine matches (?i)Start-Process.*\.(bat|cmd|ps1|exe)
Sysmon EID 1 commandLine contains '& {Start-Process' (script-block style invocation from Invoke-AtomicTest)
